title: The Pennsylvania Line mutinies at the Continental Army's camp
description: Soldiers of the Pennsylvania Line under Anthony Wayne rose in mutiny at the Continental Army's winter camp in Morristown, New Jersey, demanding higher pay and better housing. A negotiated settlement ended it, the most successful such revolt of the war.

title: Lenape and Wyandot warriors kill settlers at Big Bottom
description: Lenape and Wyandot warriors killed American settlers near present-day Stockport, Ohio, in the Big Bottom massacre. It was part of the Northwest Indian War, in which Native peoples of the Ohio Country fought to expel the settlers from their land.

title: Brazilian and Colorado forces capture Paysandú in Uruguay
description: Brazilian troops and the forces of Uruguay's Colorado Party took the town of Paysandú from its Uruguayan Army defenders, ending a siege begun on 3 December 1864. The Uruguayan War set the governing Blanco Party against Brazil and the Colorado Party.

title: Saint Thomas Christians swear the Coonan Cross Oath
description: At Mattancherry a large part of the Saint Thomas Christian community of Malabar publicly swore the Coonan Cross Oath. They refused to submit to the Jesuits and the Latin Catholic hierarchy, and rejected Portuguese dominance in church and secular matters.

skip: a weather record (lowest pressure of a non-tropical storm in the US): trivial for a history site

title: Solomon Northup, kidnapped into slavery, regains his freedom
description: Attorney Henry B. Northup persuaded the planter Edwin Epps not to contest the free papers of Solomon Northup, a free-born man from New York kidnapped into slavery in 1841. Back in New York, Northup published his memoir Twelve Years a Slave that year.

skip: a fraternity founded: trivial for a history site
the first performance of one Bach cantata: a minor first performance

title: Stefan Dečanski is crowned King of Serbia
description: Stefan Uroš III became King of Serbia after a struggle for the throne in which his brother, King Stefan Konstantin, was killed in battle; he went on to defeat their cousin Vladislav II too. He is known as Dečanski after the monastery of Visoki Dečani he built.

title: The Nizam cedes Malwa to the Marathas at Doraha
description: Sheltering in Bhopal from Bajirao's army and unable to hold out any longer, the Nizam signed a peace agreement at Doraha that ceded Malwa to the Marathas. The Mughals agreed to pay the equivalent of ₹5,000,000 in reparations.

title: The Bank of North America opens in Philadelphia
description: Chartered by the Congress of the Confederation on May 26, 1781, the Bank of North America opened in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. It was the first chartered bank in the United States and served as the country's first de facto central bank.

title: An earthquake devastates Dingxiang in northern China
description: A magnitude 7.25 earthquake struck Dingxiang and Xinxian counties in present-day Shanxi Province, killing at least 32,300 people across the province. In Xinzhou alone about 19,742 people died, and more than 50,000 livestock perished.

title: Aelia Eudoxia is proclaimed augusta of the Eastern Roman Empire
description: Eudoxia, wife of the emperor Arcadius, was officially given the title of augusta, which let her wear the purple paludamentum and appear on Roman coinage. How far she then dominated the court and the state has long been debated by historians.

title: Stephen the Great routs an invading Ottoman army at Vaslui
description: Outnumbered three to one, Stephen of Moldavia met Hadım Suleiman Pasha's army near Vaslui, where his hidden buglers threw the invaders into panic and flight. Alexander Mikaberidze calls it arguably one of the biggest European victories over the Ottomans.

title: Emperor Galba adopts Piso Licinianus as his heir
description: The emperor Galba adopted the nobleman Lucius Calpurnius Piso Frugi Licinianus, passing over Otho, who had expected to be adopted instead. Otho had both men murdered and became the second emperor of the Year of the Four Emperors.

title: The Qarmatians of Bahrayn sack Mecca during the Hajj
description: The Qarmatians of Bahrayn, an Isma'ili Shia militant movement centred in al-Ahsa in Eastern Arabia, sacked the Muslim holy city of Mecca amid the rituals of the Hajj. They had revolted against both the Fatimid and the Abbasid caliphates.

title: Theodora becomes sole ruler of the Byzantine Empire
description: Theodora Porphyrogenita, who had reigned as empress since 1042, became sole ruler of the Byzantine Empire until her death in August 1056. She was the last sovereign of the Macedonian dynasty, which had ruled the empire for almost 200 years.

title: Bayinnaung is formally crowned king in his capital Pegu
description: Having restored Tabinshwehti's empire, Bayinnaung was formally crowned in Pegu with the reign name Thiri Thudhamma Yaza. Over the next two decades his conquests built the largest empire in the history of Southeast Asia.

title: Francisco Caldeira Castelo Branco founds Belém on the Amazon
description: The Portuguese explorer Francisco Caldeira Castelo Branco founded the city of Belém, today the capital of Pará in Brazil, on the Amazon River delta. He served as the first Governor General of the Captaincy of Grão-Pará.

title: Octavian returns his provinces and armies to the Senate
description: Octavian publicly returned power to the Roman Senate and gave up his provinces and armies, though the soldiers stayed loyal to him. Three days later he took ten years' charge of provinces such as Hispania, Gaul and Syria, and with them most of the legions.

title: Pope Eugene IV forbids the enslavement of Christian Guanches
description: In the bull Sicut dudum, issued at Florence, Pope Eugene IV forbade the enslavement of the Guanches of the Canary Islands who had converted, or were converting, to Christianity. On pain of excommunication, such slaves were to be freed within 15 days.

title: Congress ratifies the Treaty of Paris with Great Britain
description: Meeting at the Maryland State House in Annapolis, the Confederation Congress proclaimed its ratification of the Treaty of Paris, the official end of the American Revolutionary War. The treaty recognised the colonies as free, sovereign and independent.

title: Bonaparte defeats the Austrian army at Rivoli
description: Near Rivoli, then in the Republic of Venice, the outnumbered French Army of Italy under General Napoleon Bonaparte defeated József Alvinczi's Austrians, who were trying to relieve besieged Mantua. Mantua fell in February, and France won the war that year.

title: Die Afrikaanse Patriot, the first Afrikaans newspaper, appears
description: The first issue of Die Afrikaanse Patriot, the first newspaper in the Afrikaans language, was published in Paarl. It began as a monthly magazine and became a weekly two years later.

skip: the day of Hatshepsut's death is uncertain: the article gives 16 January 1458 BC or 1457 BC, 'possibly', from a single stela

title: The Council of Nablus lays down laws for the Kingdom of Jerusalem
description: Ecclesiastical and secular lords of the crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem met in council at Nablus. The council produced the earliest surviving written laws of the kingdom, one of the Crusader states set up after the First Crusade.

title: Emperor Susenyos defeats Oromo raiders at Ebenat
description: Joined by Julius and Kifla Krestos, Emperor Susenyos I of Ethiopia defeated Oromo raiders who had entered Begemder. According to James Bruce, the Royal Chronicle of Susenyos reports 12,000 Oromo killed for only 400 of the emperor's men.

title: The French execute the Maltese patriot Dun Mikiel Xerri
description: Dun Mikiel Xerri, aged 61, was executed with other Maltese after taking part in an unsuccessful revolt to overthrow French rule under Napoleon Bonaparte. The French had taken over the Maltese archipelago from the Knights of St. John.

title: Magnentius is acclaimed emperor in place of Constans
description: The general Magnentius was acclaimed Augustus by the army in Gaul in place of the unpopular emperor Constans, whom he soon killed. Constans's brother Constantius II refused to recognise him, and three years of civil war ended with his suicide in 353.

title: The child Leo II becomes sole emperor in Constantinople
description: Leo II, made co-emperor in November 473, became sole emperor of the Eastern Roman Empire when his grandfather Leo I died of dysentery. His father Zeno was made co-emperor on 29 January, and Leo II died later that year.

title: Gratian makes Theodosius augustus to govern the East
description: With Valens killed at Adrianople, Gratian, convinced one emperor alone could not repel enemies on several fronts, made Theodosius augustus to govern the east. In 380 they issued the Edict of Thessalonica, making Nicene Christianity the only legal form.

title: Union forces win the Battle of Mill Springs in Kentucky
description: Union troops defeated Confederate forces near present-day Nancy, Kentucky, ending an early Confederate offensive in south central Kentucky. It was the Confederacy's first significant defeat of the American Civil War.

title: Pope Fabian is martyred in the Decian persecution
description: Fabian, bishop of Rome since 10 January 236, died a martyr in the Decian persecution. A dove is said to have descended on his head to mark him as the Holy Spirit's unexpected choice as pope; Cornelius succeeded him.

title: The Tây Sơn defeat a Siamese army at Rạch Gầm-Xoài Mút
description: Siamese forces sent to reinstate Nguyễn Phúc Ánh, who had taken refuge in Bangkok from the Tây Sơn rebels, were ambushed and defeated by the Tây Sơn on the Mekong, in present-day Đồng Tháp province of Vietnam.

title: Abdul Hamid I becomes Ottoman sultan in the war with Russia
description: Abdul Hamid I ascended the Ottoman throne on the day his brother Mustafa III died, and told the grand vizier at the front to continue the war against Russia. That year the Treaty of Küçük Kaynarca granted Russia territorial and religious influence.

title: The Power of Sympathy, called the first American novel, appears
description: Isaiah Thomas published William Hill Brown's epistolary novel The Power of Sympathy in Boston, at nine shillings. It sold poorly and appeared anonymously, and Brown was not identified as its author until 1894; it is widely considered the first American novel.

skip: the day is approximate: the article dates the battle to 'about 22 January' and calls the dates approximate

title: Rival miners' unions merge as the United Mine Workers of America
description: Miners of the National Progressive Union and of the Knights of Labor met to merge into the United Mine Workers of America. Its constitution demanded pay fitting the danger of the work, payment in legal tender rather than company scrip, and safe mines.

title: Ahmed I Bey abolishes slavery in Tunisia
description: Ahmed I Bey abolished slavery in Tunisia, a country whose position linked it to the main Trans-Saharan routes. In the eighteenth century, contemporary witnesses said, its caravans from Fezzan and Ghadamès carried only gold powder and slaves.

title: US Army troops commit the Marias Massacre in Montana
description: United States Army forces under Major Eugene Mortimer Baker attacked Piegan Blackfeet in Montana Territory, killing approximately 200 people, most of them women, children and older men. The Marias Massacre was part of the Indian Wars.

title: The Estates proclaim 14-year-old Matthias Corvinus king of Hungary
description: After King Ladislaus the Posthumous died unexpectedly, Michael Szilágyi persuaded the Estates to proclaim his nephew Matthias, son of John Hunyadi, king. Matthias began under his uncle's guardianship but took effective control within two weeks.

title: The University of Calcutta is founded
description: The University of Calcutta was established, the oldest multidisciplinary university of the Indian Subcontinent. At its founding its catchment area stretched from Kabul to Myanmar; today its jurisdiction covers a few districts of West Bengal.

title: Takeda Shingen crushes Tokugawa Ieyasu at Mikatagahara
description: On the plain of Mikatagahara north of Hamamatsu, Takeda Shingen's army encircled the Tokugawa-Oda force and almost totally annihilated it; many of Ieyasu's retainers were killed. Shingen was seeking a route to Kyoto in his campaign against Oda Nobunaga.

title: An earthquake centred in Friuli is felt across Europe
description: An earthquake centred in the South Alpine region of Friuli was felt across Europe; according to contemporary sources churches and houses collapsed and villages were destroyed. It struck in the same year that the Great Plague ravaged Italy.

title: The Treaty of Karlowitz ends the Great Turkish War
description: The Holy League and the Ottoman Empire concluded the Treaty of Karlowitz, ending the war that had begun with the failed Ottoman siege of Vienna in 1683. The Ottomans surrendered control of significant territories, many of them permanently.

title: A megathrust earthquake ruptures the Cascadia subduction zone
description: An earthquake with an estimated moment magnitude of 8.7–9.2 struck the Cascadia subduction zone, from mid-Vancouver Island to northern California. The plate slipped about 20 meters along a rupture about 1,000 kilometers long; Japanese records give its date.

title: Constantine VII ousts the Lekapenos brothers and rules alone
description: At the urging of their sister, the Augusta Helena, a coup removed the co-emperors Stephen and Constantine Lekapenos from power and restored sole imperial authority to Constantine VII. The brothers were sent into exile, first to Prote.

title: Charles VI barely escapes the fire of the Bal des Ardents
description: At a masquerade ball in Paris, King Charles VI danced in costume with five nobles when a torch brought in by his brother, Louis I, Duke of Orléans, set the dancers' costumes alight. Four of the dancers were killed; the king survived.

title: Kansas enters the Union as a free state
description: After the years of conflict between Free-Staters and pro-slavery settlers known as Bleeding Kansas, Kansas entered the Union as the 34th state, a free state. The Homestead Acts of 1862 brought a further influx of settlers.

title: US troops massacre a Shoshone encampment at Bear River
description: California Volunteers under Colonel Patrick Edward Connor attacked a Shoshone winter camp in present-day Franklin County, Idaho, killing an estimated 250 to 493 people. Some sources call it the US military's largest mass murder of Native Americans.

skip: the opening of a local bridge (the first across the Delaware): trivial for a history site

title: Yerba Buena is renamed San Francisco
description: Lt. Washington Allon Bartlett's proclamation renaming Yerba Buena as San Francisco took effect, months after US forces raised the American flag there in the Mexican–American War. The Gold Rush later made it the major city of the west coast.

title: Sylvester I is consecrated bishop of Rome
description: Sylvester I succeeded the late Pope Miltiades as bishop of Rome and held the see until his death on 31 December 335. He led it at an important era in the history of the Western Church, though very little is known of his life.

title: The forty-seven rōnin avenge their master by killing Kira Yoshinaka
description: A band of rōnin led by Ōishi Yoshio, chamberlain of the Akō Domain, killed Kira Yoshinaka, the adversary of their late master Asano Naganori. The Akō vendetta is among Japan's three major vengeance incidents, and Ōishi became the hero of the Chūshingura.

title: The First Peace of Thorn ends the war with the Teutonic Knights
description: Poland, Lithuania and the Teutonic Knights made peace at Thorn (Toruń), ending the war in which the Knights had been routed at Grunwald in 1410. The Knights returned Dobrzyń Land and made only temporary concessions in Samogitia; the peace was not stable.

title: Mayon's deadliest eruption buries the town of Cagsawa
description: Mayon volcano in the Philippines erupted and buried the town of Cagsawa under tephra; about 1,200 people died there in the most lethal eruption in Mayon's history. It is believed to have added to the atmospheric ash behind the Year Without a Summer in 1816.

title: The Great Heathen Army defeats Louis the Younger at Lüneburg Heath
description: At Lüneburg Heath, in today's Lower Saxony, the Norse Great Heathen Army defeated the army of King Louis the Younger. The army was a coalition of Scandinavian warriors, mainly from Denmark, that had invaded England in 865.

title: Pope John XII crowns Otto I Holy Roman Emperor
description: In Rome, Pope John XII solemnly crowned Otto I emperor. Soon after, Otto's Diploma Ottonianum confirmed the Roman Church in its possessions, while the pope accepted that Otto and his heirs would have a vote in the nomination of popes.

title: An earthquake devastates the region of Algiers
description: The largest shock of a seismic sequence lasting from February to May struck the Algiers region with an estimated moment magnitude of 7.0, killing approximately 20,000 people. It was felt as far away as Catania and Syracuse in Sicily.

title: Ramon Berenguer III of Barcelona marries Douce of Provence
description: At Arles, Ramon Berenguer III, Count of Barcelona, married Douce I, who had that year inherited the county of Provence through her mother. He was count of Provence as well from then until his death in Barcelona in 1131.

title: Emperor Septimius Severus dies at Eboracum
description: Septimius Severus fell ill while campaigning in Caledonia and died at Eboracum (modern York), said to have advised his sons: "Be harmonious, enrich the soldiers, scorn all others." His sons Caracalla and Geta succeeded him.

title: Sebastião Veiga Cabral founds São José de Macapá
description: Under the authority of the governor of Pará, Sebastião Veiga Cabral founded the town of São José de Macapá, where a Portuguese military detachment had been stationed since 1738. Macapá, on the Amazon delta, is today the capital of Amapá.

title: A conclave at Perugia elects Gui Foucois as Pope Clement IV
description: After four months of argument over whether to call in Charles of Anjou to carry on the papal war against the Hohenstaufens, the cardinals at Perugia elected Gui Foucois pope. As Clement IV he was a patron of Thomas Aquinas and Roger Bacon.

title: French armies begin the siege of Cádiz
description: After occupying Seville, 70,000 French troops under Marshals Claude Victor and Jean-de-Dieu Soult laid siege to Cádiz, which had become the Spanish seat of power. Defended by Spanish, British and Portuguese troops, it held out until August 1812.

title: Julius I becomes bishop of Rome
description: Julius I became bishop of Rome, holding the see until his death in 352. He backed Athanasius when Arian bishops deposed him, asserted the pope's authority over the Arian Eastern bishops, and is credited with setting December 25 as the birthdate of Jesus.

title: Dandara of Palmares takes her life rather than return to slavery
description: Dandara, a warrior of the Quilombo dos Palmares, a settlement of Afro-Brazilians who had freed themselves from slavery, was arrested and killed herself rather than return to it. Little is known of her; she and Zumbi, last king of Palmares, had three children.

title: Thihathu founds the Pinya Kingdom as heir to Pagan
description: Thihathu, who with his brothers had defended central Burma from the Mongols, proclaimed himself successor of the Pagan dynasty and founded the Pinya Kingdom, moving his capital from Pinle to Pinya. The kingdom ruled central Burma until 1365.

title: The states ratify the Eleventh Amendment to the US Constitution
description: The states ratified the Eleventh Amendment, which Congress had passed on March 4, 1794. It restricts the ability of individuals to bring suit in federal court against states of which they are not citizens.
source: Eleventh Amendment to the United States Constitution

title: Honorius makes his general Constantius III co-emperor
description: Honorius proclaimed Constantius III, his magister militum and the husband of his sister Galla Placidia, co-emperor in the West. Constantius had put down the usurper Constantine III and recovered much of Hispania and Gaul, but reigned only seven months.

title: The Senate elects Richard Mentor Johnson vice president
description: Virginia's 23 faithless electors left Richard Mentor Johnson one electoral vote short of a majority, so for the only time the Senate chose the vice president, electing him by 33 votes to 16 for Francis Granger. He served under Martin Van Buren.

title: Bohemond's knights rout Radwan of Aleppo near Antioch
description: As the Crusaders besieged Antioch, Bohemond of Taranto gathered all the remaining horses and marched by night against a relief army led by Radwan, the Seljuq ruler of Aleppo. After several cavalry charges the knights routed it, forcing Radwan back to Aleppo.

skip: one state's ratification of the Articles of Confederation (the fourth of thirteen): a minor procedural step

title: A tavern quarrel starts the St Scholastica Day riot in Oxford
description: Two Oxford students' complaint about the wine at the Swindlestock Tavern became a riot lasting three days, with armed gangs from the countryside joining the townspeople. Around twenty townsfolk and up to sixty-three members of the university were killed.

title: Union vessels destroy the Confederate Mosquito Fleet
description: After the Battle of Roanoke Island, ships of the US Navy's North Atlantic Blockading Squadron attacked the Confederate Mosquito Fleet on the Pasquotank River near Elizabeth City, North Carolina. The Union took the town and the fleet was destroyed.

title: Fastolf's convoy beats off the French at the Battle of the Herrings
description: Near Rouvray, north of Orléans, French and Scottish forces under Charles of Bourbon and Sir John Stewart of Darnley attacked a supply convoy bound for the English army besieging the city. Its escort under Sir John Fastolf won decisively.

title: The Creek cede their last Georgia lands at Indian Springs
description: By the Treaty of Indian Springs, concluded with the United States, the Muscogee (Creek) ceded the last of their lands in Georgia to the US government and migrated west. An additional article was added to the treaty two days later.

title: The central tower of Ely Cathedral collapses
description: In the night, possibly because of digging for the Lady Chapel's foundations, the Norman central crossing tower of Ely Cathedral collapsed. It was replaced by a far larger open octagon, built under Alan of Walsingham, the cathedral's most distinctive feature.

title: Genoa's fleet wins a night battle in the Bosporus
description: Fought largely at night in a storm, the battle between Genoa's fleet and the allied fleets of Venice, Aragon and the Byzantine Empire left Genoa the victor. Emperor John VI Kantakouzenos then made terms with Genoa and left the War of the Straits.

title: Abu Muslim's rebels take Merv, capital of Khorasan
description: Abu Muslim, who had risen openly against Umayyad rule under the Black Standard the previous June, took control of Merv and expelled the governor Nasr ibn Sayyar. His armies then pushed west in the revolution that overthrew the Umayyad Caliphate.

title: Ibrahim ibn Abdallah dies, ending the Alid revolt
description: Wounded when Isa ibn Musa's Abbasid troops scattered his army at Bāchamrā south of Kufa, Ibrahim ibn Abdallah died there, ending the revolt he had led after his brother. The caliph al-Mansur then had supporters such as Abu Hanifa imprisoned.

title: Theodosius II publishes the Codex Theodosianus
description: A constitution of Theodosius II published the Codex Theodosianus, a compilation of the laws made by the Christian emperors from 311 to 437, begun by a commission of 429. It went into force in both parts of the empire on 1 January 439.

skip: a football club founded: trivial for a history site

title: An earthquake and megatsunami strike Ambon Island
description: An earthquake in the Maluku Islands raised a tsunami up to 100 metres high on Ambon Island, killing over 2,000 people. It was the first detailed documentation of a tsunami in Indonesia and the largest recorded there; a submarine landslide was likely the cause.

title: The Lancastrian army wins at St Albans and frees Henry VI
description: In the second battle fought at St Albans, Hertfordshire, the Lancastrian army defeated the Yorkist army and released King Henry VI from captivity. The Wars of the Roses were fought between the houses of York and Lancaster for the English throne.

title: Spain's Armada of Flanders strikes an Anglo-Dutch convoy
description: Off the coast of Cornwall, Admiral Miguel de Horna's Armada of Flanders intercepted an Anglo-Dutch merchant convoy of 44 vessels escorted by six Dutch warships, sinking or capturing 20 ships, and returned safely to its base at Dunkirk.

skip: the material says only that Boniface III was pope for a few months and made 'a significant contribution', without saying what

title: Yohannan Sulaqa makes a Catholic profession of faith in Rome
description: Yohannan Sulaqa, who had travelled to Rome to be confirmed as patriarch, made a profession of faith before Pope Julius III and was consecrated bishop in April. He was the first patriarch of what became the Shemʿon line of the Chaldean Catholic Church.
